elements.element: Customer is not prohibited from participating in competing or similar projects.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 expressly prohibits the Company for twelve months from participating in any similar Internet project involving Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Vendor is not granted an exclusive or sole-supplier right that binds or restricts Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 grants HDI the exclusive right to use the “Deerskin” brand for a self-contained consumer website offering Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restriction is confined to the capitalized category “Deerskin Products”; the original extension to products “substantially similar” to Deerskin Products has been removed.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity lasts no more than twelve months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 applies only “for a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date,” notwithstanding the Agreement’s renewal provisions.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity terminates automatically if Vendor fails to meet a service level.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 states that it “shall terminate automatically if HDI fails to meet any service level” under the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer exclusivity terminates automatically if Vendor fails to meet a delivery date.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 states that it “shall terminate automatically if HDI fails to meet ... any delivery date” under the Agreement.

result.reason: The operative clause retains exclusivity and therefore does not satisfy the preferred position. It does satisfy every fallback element: the restriction is confined to Deerskin Products, lasts twelve months, and terminates automatically upon HDI’s failure to meet any service level or delivery date. The changes are limited to those needed for the fallback and do not alter unrelated termination or exception provisions.
